t: LeetCode 3231 – Minimum Number of Increasing Subsequence to Be Removed
o: Repeatedly delete a strictly increasing subsequence until the array is empty; minimize the number of deletions. By Dilworth's theorem, the minimum number of strictly increasing sequences needed to partition a sequence equals the length of its longest non-increasing subsequence. Check: [5,3,1,4,2] has longest non-increasing 5,3,1 (length 3) → answer 3; a fully decreasing array needs n removals; a fully increasing array needs 1. So the task reduces to computing the longest non-increasing subsequence, solvable in O(n log n) with patience-style binary search.
k: Dilworth duality: min strictly-increasing subsequences to cover = longest weakly decreasing subsequence.
Negate values and compute the longest non-decreasing subsequence with bisect_right.

a.n: Approach 1: Patience sorting with binary search
a.i: Maintain tails for the longest non-decreasing subsequence of the negated array. For each x, binary-search (bisect_right, allowing equality) for the first tail ≥ x and replace it, or append. The final pile count is the answer.
s: For each num: y = -num; find pos = bisect_right(tails, y).
Replace tails[pos] or append; return len(tails).
a.t: O(n log n) — one binary search per element

a.i: Direct application of the characterization: dp[i] = length of the longest non-increasing subsequence ending at i, i.e. 1 + max over j < i with nums[j] ≥ nums[i]. The answer is the maximum dp. Clear but O(n²).
s: For each j < i with nums[j] >= nums[i], dp[i] = max(dp[i], dp[j] + 1).
a.t: O(n²) — all ordered pairs examined; fine for small n, slow at 10^5

w: Always quote Dilworth's theorem — it converts an unfamiliar covering problem into a standard LIS variant instantly. Pitfall: the removed subsequences are strictly increasing, so the dual allows EQUAL elements in the decreasing subsequence (use ≥ comparisons / bisect_right, not bisect_left). Edge cases: single element → 1; all equal → n. Follow-up: minimum number of non-decreasing subsequences (dual becomes strictly decreasing), or reconstructing the actual subsequences.
